title: Cc No. 512564/16 Kamal Kumar vs . Rajesh Saini Page No. 1/13 on 11 December, 2019
full_text: Cc No. 512564/16 Kamal Kumar vs . Rajesh Saini Page No. 1/13 on 11 December, 2019 IN THE COURT OF MS. NAINA METROPOLITAN MAGISTRATE (N.I. Act) -07 TIS HAZARI COURTS, CENTRAL DISTRICT, NEW DELHI Sh. Kamal Kumar S/o Late Sh. Prabhu Dayal R/o S-1/17, Tibbia College Quarter, Karol Bagh, New Delhi. .............. Complainant VERSUS Sh. Rajesh Saini S/o Sh. Randhir Singh R/o 84/1, 1st Floor, Land Mark, Near Maghav Bhawan Village, Khurani, New Delhi-110040 ............. Accused New Case Number. : 512564/16 Date of Institution of Case : 28.08.2015 Offence Complained Of. : 138 NI Act Plea of the Accused. : Pleaded not guilty Arguments Heard On. : 21.10.2019 Date of Judgment. : 11.12.2019 CC No. 512564/16 Kamal Kumar Vs. Rajesh Saini Page no. 1/13 :: JUDGMENT : : Facts 1. The case of the complainant is that the complainant was running a joint business with the accused in the name and style of Saini Refrigeration and they are known to each other. It is stated that in the year 2013, the accused and the complainant wanted to built up the business to high extent and in this regard money was required and for the same, the accused requested the complainant to invest some money in the business and assured the complainant either to return the said money to the complainant or to adjust the said amount by deducting in the profits. It is stated that on the assurance of the accused, the complainant spent a sum of Rs. 9,58,850/- and thereafter the complainant time and again requested the accused to return the said amount but the accused neither returned the said amount nor gave extra profit to the complainant as agreed by him before investment. It is stated that after lot of request made by the complainant, the accused in discharge of their legal liability issued cheque bearing no. 915983 dated 05.06.2015 for sum of Rs. 9,58,850/- drawn on Corporation Bank, Branch of Narela, New Delhi in favour of complainant. 2. The complainant presented the said cheque on the assurance of the accused and the cheque was returned unpaid with remarks "Funds Insufficient" vide memo dated 09.06.2015. Thereafter, complainant has sent legal notice dated 12.06.2015 to the accused for paying the amount of the CC No. 512564/16 Kamal Kumar Vs. Rajesh Saini Page no. 2/13 cheque but despite service of notice, payment was not made. Hence, the complaint was filed. 3. To prove his case, the complainant has examined himself as CW1 and led on record the following documents to prove the liability of the accused :- a) Ex. CW-1/A : Evidence by way of affidavit. b) Ex. CW-1/1 : Original cheque. c) Ex. CW-1/2 : Returning memo d) Ex. CW-1/3 : Legal notice. e) Ex. CW-1/4 : Postal receipt of speed post. 4. On summoning, the accused entered his appearance and notice was framed on 28.01.2016, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. He stated that cheque in question has been issued by him as security for loan of Rs.1 lac advanced by the complainant to him. He stated that he has repaid this loan and he has no liability towards the cheque in question. 5. After the framing of notice the complainant was recalled for cross examination and his cross examination was completed on 10.12.2018. 6. After the completion of complainant evidence, the accused was examined u/s 313 Cr.P.C. In his examination u/s 313 Cr.P.C, the accused reiterated his defence and stated that he has already repaid the loan amount of about Rs. 1,25,000/- to the complainant. The complainant did not return his cheque even after receiving the entire loan amount with interest. 7. The accused has examined himself as DW-1 in his defence. CC No. 512564/16 Kamal Kumar Vs. Rajesh Saini Page no. 3/13 8. I have heard arguments led on behalf of both the sides. 9. To make any person liable under Section 138 Negotiable Instruments Act (hereinafter to be read as ' The Act '), the following ingredients are required to be proved by the complainant: (i) Person must have drawn a cheque on an account maintained by him in a bank for payment of a certain amount of money to another person from out of that account; (ii) The cheque should have been issued for the discharge, in whole or in part, of any debt or other liability; (iii)That cheque has been presented to the bank within a period of six months from the date on which it is drawn or within the period of its validity whichever is earlier; (iv)That cheque is returned by the bank unpaid, either because of the amount of money standing to the credit of the account is insufficient to honour the cheque or that it exceeds the amount arranged to be paid from that account by an agreement made with the bank; (v) The payee or the holder in due course of the cheque makes a demand for the payment of the said amount of money by giving a notice in writing, to the drawer of the cheque, within 30 days of the receipt of information by him from the bank regarding the return of the cheque as unpaid; (vi) The drawer of such cheque fails to make payment of the said amount of money to the payee or the holder in due course of the cheque within 15 days of the receipt of the said notice. 10. The complainant has filed on record cheque no. 915983 (hereinafter cheque in question) dated 05.06.2015 for a sum of Rs.9,58,850/-. He has also filed return memo dated 09.06.2015 which is Ex. CW-1/2 as per which cheque bearing no. 915983 was returned back unpaid with the remarks "Funds Insufficient". The complainant sent a legal notice to the accused dated 12.06.2015 within 30 days of the knowledge of the return of the cheque but no payment was made as per the legal notice. Accordingly, cause of action arose CC No. 512564/16 Kamal Kumar Vs. Rajesh Saini Page no. 4/13 in favour of the complainant and the present complaint was filed. All the ingredients of Section 138 of NI Act as discussed above have been met with in this case. 11. The accused has admitted the issuance of the cheque in question to the complainant and also his signatures on the cheque in question. Once these facts that the cheque in question belongs to the accused and the signatures on the cheque in question are of the accused are established, a presumption of the cheque having been issued in discharge of a legally sustainable liability and drawn for good consideration, arises by virtue of Section 118 (a) and Section 139 of the NI Act. Once the Section 139 of NI Act comes into picture, the court presumes that the cheque was issued in discharge, in whole or in part, of any debt or other liability. At this stage, with the help of the presumption under Section 139 of the Act, the case of the complainant stands proved. 12. When the presumption is raised in favor of the complainant, the burden shifts upon the accused to disprove the case of the complainant by rebutting the presumption raised in favour of the complainant. Being the rule of reverse onus, it is the duty on the accused to prove that he does not owe any liability towards the complainant. The accused can displace this presumption on the scale of preponderance of probabilities and the lack of consideration or a legally enforceable debt need not be proved beyond all reasonable doubts. The accused has to make out a fairly plausible defence which is acceptable to CC No. 512564/16 Kamal Kumar Vs. Rajesh Saini Page no. 5/13 the court. This the accused can do either by leading own evidence in his defence or by raising doubt on the material/evidence brought on the record by the complainant. 13. The accused has admitted the issuance of the cheque in question to the complainant. The defence of the accsued is that the cheque in question was issued in blank as a security to the complainant for availing a loan of Rs. 1 lakh only from the complainant. The accused has contended that the accsued has already repaid Rs. 1,25,000/- to the complainant inclusive of the loan amount and the interest. It is stated that the accused has no legal debt or liability towards the complainant. DEFENCE THAT THE CHEQUE IN QUESTION WAS ISSUED IN BLANK 14. The accused has contended that he has not filled in the particulars in the cheque. The complainant in his cross examination has stated, "I do not remember whether the cheque was completely filled up or not. (Vol. The amount was filled up and I do not remember whether the date was filled up and the cheque was filled up in the presence of accused's cousin)." It is contended on behalf of the accused that the cheque in question was issued in blank as security only. In the present case, the accused has admitted that he had given the cheque in question to the complainant after signing the same. It is settled law that if any blank cheque is issued; it is issued with an implied authority to the drawee to fill in other particulars such as date or amount CC No. 512564/16 Kamal Kumar Vs. Rajesh Saini Page no. 6/13 correspondent to the liability on the part of the drawer. Sections 20 and 118 of the Negotiable Instruments Act are relevant in this context. 15. Further, reliance is placed upon the judgment of the Honb'le High Court of Delhi in the case of Mojji Engineering Systems Limited & Ors. Vs. A.B. Sugars Ltd. ; 154 (2008) Delhi Law Times 579 wherein it was observed that when a blank cheque is signed and handed over, it means the person signing it has given an implied authority to any subsequent holder to fill it up. Recently, the Supreme Court in the case of Bir Singh Vs. Mukesh Kumar AIR 2019 SC 2446 observed, "It is immaterial that the cheque may have been filled in by any person other than the drawer, if the cheque is duly signed by the drawer. If the cheque is otherwise valid, the penal provision of Section 138 would be attracted. If a signed blank cheque is voluntarily presented to a payee, towards some payment, the payee may fill up the amount and other particulars. This in itself would not invalidate the cheque. The onus would be still on the accused to prove that the cheque was not in discharge of a debt or liability by adducing evidence." 16. In view of the discussion above, the defence of the accused that he has not filled in the particulars in the cheque is untenable. It is assumed that the accused had given an implied authority to the complainant to fill the amount in the cheque at the time of issuing of blank cheque. Thus, the contention that the particulars in the cheque in question have not been filled in by the accused is not acceptable. It is further presumed that the cheque in question was CC No. 512564/16 Kamal Kumar Vs. Rajesh Saini Page no. 7/13 issued in discharge of a legal debt or liability. The accused must rebut the presumption in favour of the complainant and prove on preponderance of probabilities that there is no legal debt or liability outstanding towards the complainant. DEFENCE THAT THE CHEQUE IN QUESTION WAS ISSUED AS SECURITY 17. The accused has taken the defence that the cheque in question was issued only as a security at the time of taking of loan of Rs. 1 lakh from the complainant and the accused has already repaid the loan amount to the complainant. It is contended that the cheque in question was not issued towards any outstanding debt or liability. The Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the case of Suresh Chandra Goyal Vs. Amit Singhal has held that section 138 NI Act covers any cheque drawn on an account maintained by the drawer with the bank in favour of another person for the discharge of any debt or other liability. The expression 'any debt or other liability' is unqualified in section 138 NI Act and it includes any future debt or liability which may arise after the issuance of the cheque. It was observed that section 138 NI Act does not distinguish between a cheque issued by the debtor in discharge of an existing debt or other liability, or a cheque issued as a security cheque on the premise that on the due future date the debt which shall have crystallized by then, shall be paid. So long as there is a debt existing, in respect whereof the cheque in question is issued, the same would attract Section 138 of NI Act in case of its dishonour. Thus, mere defence that the cheque in question was issued as a CC No. 512564/16 Kamal Kumar Vs. Rajesh Saini Page no. 8/13 security cheque is not sufficient. The accused must show that there was no legal debt or liability outstanding towards the complainant. DEFENCE THAT THE ACCUSED HAS NO LEGAL DEBT OR LIABILITY TOWARDS THE COMPLAINANT 18. This court must now examine whether the accused is able to prove that there was no debt or liability outstanding against the complainant at the time of presentation of the cheque in question, on the standard of preponderance of probabilities. Under section 139 NI Act, It is presumed that the cheque in question was issued in discharge of legal debt or liability. The defence of the accused is that he had taken a loan of Rs. 1 lakh only from the complainant against the cheque as security. It is stated that the loan has already been repaid by him to the complainant along with interest. To establish his defence the accused has himself entered the witness box. 19. DW-1, the accused in his chief examination has stated that he asked the complainant to lend him Rs. 1 lakh against security cheque and thereafter he has returned the amount to the complainant alongwith interest @2% p.m. but complainant demanded interest @6% p.m. and due to this dispute arose with the complainant. In his cross-examination he has stated that he has not filed any complaint till date against the complainant for threatening to file a case against him. He does not have any receipt of payment of Rs. 1 lakh made to the complainant. He also stated it to be correct that he does not have any prove that he borrowed money from the complainant at interest. A document CC No. 512564/16 Kamal Kumar Vs. Rajesh Saini Page no. 9/13 Ex. CW1/5 was put to the accused wherein the accused has stated that he has received Rs.9,58,850/- as friendly loan from the complainant and he shall return it to the complainant as soon as possible. This document is a cash receipt dated 13.02.2014. The accused in his cross-examination denied his signatures on the document Ex. CW1/5 and also denied execution of the same. 20. The accused apart from examining himself has not led any other evidence to support his defence that he had given the cheque in question as security for obtaining a loan of Rs. 1,00,000/- only. There is nothing on record to prove the loan transaction of Rs. 1,00,000/- and return of the same amount to the complainant. The accused could have raised a probable defence either by leading his own evidence or by pointing out inconsistencies in the case of the complainant. The testimony of the complainant is also examined below. 21. The Ld. Counsel for the accused has cross examined the complainant at length. The complainant has unequivocally denied the suggestions of the Ld. Counsel for the accused that the complainant was a money lender and he had given a loan of Rs. 1 lakh to the accused and the accused issued a security cheque to him. The Ld. Counsel for the accused has put questions to the complainant about the transactions between the parties. The complainant stated that he was sentenced to imprisonment for 10 years and he was released from jail after serving 7 years of imprisonment. Since, the accused was known to him for a long time, after serving the sentence he started CC No. 512564/16 Kamal Kumar Vs. Rajesh Saini Page no. 10/13 working with the accused. He stated that he worked with the accused for around 4-5 years and he paid the cheque amount within first three years of the partnership. It is stated by the complainant that he gave around Rs. 10 lakh in cash to the complainant and the money was given after selling of a plot by the complainant. He has also stated that the plot was purchased prior to 2002 and the same was informed to his employer and the same was purchased in installments. The complainant in his cross-examination has explained the manner in which money was given to the accused and also the source from which money was procured. There is no contradiction in the testimony of the complainant regarding the transaction as averred by him in the complaint. 22. It has been argued on behalf of the accused that the complainant has not placed on record any document regarding the sale of his plot. It is to be noted that the initial burden of proving that the accused has no liability towards the complainant is on the accused himself. Therefore, the complainant need not have led any positive evidence to prove the liability of the accused. The complainant has explained the source of money for giving it to the accused in his cross examination. 23. The complainant in his cross examination stated that he gave money to the accused as the accused was being harassed by the local money lenders and also because the complainant had good relations with the accused. He stated that he did not get any profit from the business but he still invested money because of good family relations with the accused. The accused CC No. 512564/16 Kamal Kumar Vs. Rajesh Saini Page no. 11/13 himself has also stated that the complainant was known to him for the last 14 to 15 years and they have been friends. It has also been admitted by the accused that he had approached the complainant for loan. Thus, the acquaintance between the parties and the financial need of the accused person has been established in this case. Ld. Counsel for the accused has argued that there is a discrepancy in the version of the complainant as the complainant in his complaint has stated that he had invested in the business of the accused and in document Ex. CW-15 it is stated that it was a friendly loan. The case of the complainant is that the accused had requested the complainant to invest some money in his business and assured the complainant either to return the said money to the complainant or to adjust the said amount by deducting profits. Since no profit were made, the complainant had asked for the return of the money. There is a slight difference in the terminology used by the complainant but the transaction in essence is a loan transaction where the complainant had given money to the accused with the promise of return. Therefore, there is no material discrepancy in the case of the complainant. 24. The complainant in his cross examination could not state the date when the cheque was given by the accused to him. He has stated that he does not remember the date when the cheque was given to him by the accused. In this case the issuance of the cheque by the accused to the complainant has been admitted. Therefore, the issuance of the cheque itself is not in dispute. CC No. 512564/16 Kamal Kumar Vs. Rajesh Saini Page no. 12/13 25. In view of the aforesaid reasons, the court finds that the accused has not been able to prove any probable defence that there was no legal liability or debt against the accused. The accused could not probablise his defence that the cheque in question was issued as security for a loan of Rs. 1 lakh only and the same has been repaid by the accused to the complainant. The accused has failed to rebut the presumption raised U/s. 139 of the NI Act , there is no need to go into complainant's evidence for proving the complainant's case. There is nothing coming out in the cross examination of complainant's witness which would probablise the defence raised by the accused or falsify the case of the complainant. Therefore, the complainant has been able to prove his case beyond reasonable doubt. 26. The complainant has been able to prove that the cheque in question i.e. cheque bearing no. 915983 dated 05.06.2015 for Rs.9,58,850/- drawn on Corporation Bank, Narela Branch, New Delhi Ex.CW1/1 was issued in discharge of legally recoverable liability owed to the complainant by the accused. 27. Therefore, the accused Rajesh Saini is convicted for the offence punishable U/s. 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act in respect of cheque Ex Digitally signed by CW1/1.
